About the tune

  • Melody: Negro Spiritual
  • Arranged (1907): Frederick J. Work (died 1942)
  • Arranged (1907): John W. Work, Jr. (1871–1925)

Metre: Irregular.

Melody from the Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (CCEH, public domain); tune SOMEBODY'S KNOCKING (Negro Spiritual). The CCEH gives its tunes as four-part scores; this page has the melody only, read from its MIDI file and checked against its incipit, and NoteFusion's engine wrote the solfa from the notes. It has not yet been checked against a printed hymn book. The arranger named above set CCEH's harmony, which is not shown here.

Questions about Somebody's Knocking

What is the doh of Somebody's Knocking?

In this version, in Eb major, doh is Eb. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Somebody's Knocking start on?

It starts on d (E♭ in Eb major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to d.

Is Somebody's Knocking in the public domain?

Yes. Frederick J. Work died in 1942, John W. Work, Jr. died in 1925; the tune was first published in 1907. Everyone named died before 1955 and it was published before 1929, so the tune is out of copyright in Nigeria, the UK, the EU and the United States. Modern arrangements of it can still be under copyright.
